item.dc:creator: Adam Cron

item.title: What Is Automotive Virtualization?
item.dc:creator: Mohit Bhardwaj

item.title: What is a Data Center? Architecture, Types & AI Evolution
item.dc:creator: Larry Williams
item.description: Learn how modern data centers are designed for performance and efficiency, from core infrastructure and cooling to AI-driven innovation.

item.title: What is an Electronics Digital Twin?
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: An Electronics Digital Twin (eDT) is a virtual representation of an electronic system and its environment.

item.title: What is a Digital Twin? Definition, Types, and Examples
item.dc:creator: Raja Badrinarayanan
item.description: Learn how digital twins use real-time data to model physical systems, improving performance, decision-making, and operational efficiency.

item.title: What is ADAS? Advanced Driver Assistance Systems Explained
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Follin, Sr
item.description: Learn the types and components of advanced driver assistance systems, how ADAS technology is developed and validated, and its role in vehicle safety.

item.title: What is Voltage Drop?
item.dc:creator: Marc Swinnen
item.description: What is voltage drop? Learn the voltage drop formula, how to calculate voltage drop in DC and AC circuits, and how engineers reduce IR drop.

item.title: What is Automatic Test Equipment?
item.dc:creator: Adam Cron
item.description: Learn what Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) is, related system components, benefits, and how it is used across industries and with simulation.

item.title: What is Physical AI?
item.dc:creator: Sumit Vishwakarma, Todd Koelling, Rich Goldman
item.description: Learn what physical AI is and how autonomous systems employ it, how it is applied across industries, and physical AI’s various challenges.

item.title: What is Electromagnetic Coupling?
item.dc:creator: Akanksha Soni
item.description: Learn how to determine the cause of electromagnetic coupling by understanding how it is coupled from source to receiver.

item.title: What Are S-parameters?
item.dc:creator: Akanksha Soni
item.description: Discover S-parameters and their role in characterizing RF, microwave, and high-speed electronic designs for accurate performance analysis.

item.title: What is Nodal Analysis?
item.dc:creator: Akanksha Soni
item.description: Learn what nodal analysis is with helpful examples, why it's important, and the six steps used to perform a nodal analysis.

item.title: What is an RLC Circuit?
item.dc:creator: Akanksha Soni
item.description: Understanding RLC circuits is critical to the design and analysis of circuits that are used in a wide range of electronics and communications systems.

item.title: What is a Microchip?
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: Learn about microchips, integrated circuits, and semiconductor technology powering the devices, systems, and innovations we use every day.

item.title: What is Advanced Semiconductor Packaging?
item.description: Learn more about advanced semiconductor packaging and different types of advanced packaging technologies to gain a competitive advantage in the market.

item.title: What is a Mixed-Signal Integrated Circuit?
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: Explore mixed-signal IC design and how it enables efficient integration of analog and digital functions in modern electronic devices.

item.title: What is Register-Transfer-Level (RTL) Design?
item.description: Find out about RTL design, its role in integrated circuit design, the steps involved in RTL design flow, and how it applies to semiconductor chips.

item.title: What is a System on a Chip (SoC)?
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: A system on a chip is an integrated circuit that compresses all of a system’s required components onto one piece of silicon.

item.title: What is AI Chip Design? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Todd Koelling
item.description: An AI chip is built for efficient AI workloads, delivering high performance and energy savings for data centers, edge devices, and AI factories.

item.title: What is AI-Driven Chip Design?
item.dc:creator: Todd Koelling
item.description: AI-driven chip design uses AI to optimize semiconductor performance, power, and area, exploring more options than possible manually.

item.title: What is EDA Agentic AI? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Rob van Blommestein
item.description: EDA Agentic AI uses autonomous multi-agent systems to optimize chip design workflows, boost engineering productivity, and accelerate innovation.

item.title: What is Lithography? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Claris Leung
item.description: Learn how lithography drives semiconductor manufacturing by patterning intricate features on silicon wafers for modern electronic devices.

item.title: What is Logic Design? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Frank Malloy
item.description: Digital logic design creates circuits using binary signals and logic gates, enabling reliable computing, AI, and control applications.

item.title: What is Physical Design? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Frank Malloy
item.description: Physical design is the process of converting logic design into a chip layout, including placement, routing, and verification for manufacturable silicon chips.

item.title: What is Place and Route? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Frank Malloy
item.description: Explore Place and Route in silicon chip design and see how electronic design automation tools optimize placement, routing, and performance.

item.title: What is PPA (Power, Performance, and Area)?
item.dc:creator: Frank Malloy
item.description: In silicon chip design, PPA represents Power, Performance, and Area. These are key metrics used to evaluate the quality and efficiency of a silicon chip design.

item.title: What is Simulation in Chip Design and Verification?
item.dc:creator: Khalid Khan
item.description: Explore simulation techniques in EDA, from logic verification to power and fault analysis, for accurate IC and SoC development.

item.title: What is Verification? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Khalid Khan
item.description: Verification ensures hardware and software designs meet specifications and operate as intended, reducing risk and improving product quality.

item.title: What is Synthesis? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Khalid Khan
item.description: Learn how synthesis converts hardware descriptions into optimized gate-level designs for efficient chip implementation and production.

item.title: What is HAV Prototyping? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Khalid Khan
item.description: Learn how HAV prototyping accelerates system validation and verification with scalable hardware-assisted solutions for faster development.

item.title: What is HAV Emulation? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Khalid Khan
item.description: Learn how HAV emulation accelerates validation of complex designs with hardware-assisted verification, enabling faster, more reliable silicon development.

item.title: What is Design for Test (DFT)? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Claris Leung
item.description: Design for Test (DFT) refers to a set of design techniques that make integrated circuits easier to test for manufacturing defects and operational faults.

item.title: What is Edge AI? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Scott Knowlton
item.description: Edge AI enables real-time AI processing and decision-making directly on devices, reducing latency, improving privacy, and minimizing cloud dependence.

item.title: What is a Silicon Die? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Frank Malloy
item.description: A silicon die is the semiconductor foundation of integrated circuits, powering everything from smartphones and automotive systems to data centers.

item.title: What is Root of Trust? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Vincent van der Leest
item.description: Root of Trust combines hardware and software security foundations to protect data, verify authenticity, and defend against cyber threats.

item.title: What is an Integrated Circuit (IC)? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Rob van Blommestein, Sumit Vishwakarma
item.description: Learn how integrated circuits (ICs) combine electronic components on a single chip to power modern devices with high performance and efficiency.

item.title: What is ASIC Design? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Rob van Blommestein, Sumit Vishwakarma
item.description: Learn how ASIC design enables custom semiconductor solutions built for specific applications, delivering optimized efficiency and performance.

item.title: What is an FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array)? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Ian Land, Khalid Khan
item.description: Learn how FPGAs provide reconfigurable hardware that enables rapid development, flexibility, and performance across a wide range of applications.

item.title: What is Functional Verification? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Taruna Reddy
item.description: Functional verification ensures your chip behaves as intended. Explore key tools, techniques, and tips to improve reliability and reduce rework.

item.title: What is Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Vincent van der Leest
item.description: Learn how Post-Quantum Cryptography safeguards sensitive information with quantum-resistant algorithms designed for the next era of security.

item.title: What are Chiplets? – How Do Chiplets Work?
item.dc:creator: Soheil Modirzadeh
item.description: Learn how chiplets enable modular semiconductor design, delivering greater flexibility, performance, and efficiency for advanced multi-die design.

item.title: What is a Physical Unclonable Function (PUF)? – How it Works
item.dc:creator: Vincent van der Leest
item.description: Discover how silicon PUF technology uses intrinsic hardware variations to create secure, unclonable identities for microprocessors and ICs.

item.title: What is SRAM PUF (Static Random-Access Memory Physical Unclonable Function)?
item.dc:creator: Vincent van der Leest
item.description: Learn how SRAM PUF technology creates hardware-based cryptographic keys using intrinsic silicon variations for enhanced security.

item.title: What is a Process Design Kit and How Does it Work?
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: A Process Design Kit (PDK) is a library of basic photonic components generated by the foundry to give open access to their generic process for fabrication.

item.title: What is Power Optimization?
item.dc:creator: Rob van Blommestein
item.description: Learn how power optimization improves energy efficiency in digital designs while maintaining performance, functionality, safety, and security.

item.title: What is High Bandwidth Memory 3 (HBM3)?
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: HBM3 is a high-bandwidth memory standard that delivers significant performance and efficiency improvements through advanced 3D-stacked DRAM technology.

item.title: What is Universal Flash Storage (UFS)? – How Does it Work?
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: Learn how UFS delivers fast, efficient storage for mobile devices, enabling improved performance, responsiveness, and power efficiency.

item.title: What are Atomistic Simulations? – Methods & Advantages
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: Learn how atomistic simulations predict material properties and interactions at the atomic level for chemistry, electronics, and materials science.

item.title: What are Machine-Learned Force Fields and How Does It Work?
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: Discover machine-learned force fields, a data-driven approach that accelerates accurate atomic-scale simulations for materials research and device design.

item.title: What is RISC-V? – How Does it Work?
item.dc:creator: Synopsys Editorial Staff
item.description: RISC-V is an open-source instruction set architecture used to develop custom processors for a variety of applications, from embedded designs to supercomputers.
